clue.text: Designing boat with funny stern

parts.note: a craft is a boat or vessel

indicators.note: the stern is the back end of a boat, so here the final letter of the word funny

explanation.surface: Someone sketching plans for a vessel with a comical rear end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stern' keeps up the boating picture but takes the last letter of 'funny', Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A designing person is scheming and cunning, the same as a wily one.

clue.text: Flower for clown's sweetheart

definitions.meaning: a garden plant with spurred blooms, also called aquilegia
in the harlequinade the beloved of Harlequin, the clown figure of pantomime

explanation.surface: A bloom picked for a clown's girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a spurred garden plant and to Harlequin's lover in pantomime.

clue.text: Pardon me! Nasty mess here

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so the letters of the two words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone begs forgiveness after making an unpleasant mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' rearranges ME and NASTY; 'here' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An official pardon granted to many offenders at once is a general reprieve.

clue.text: Salesmen, proverbially broad-minded?

definitions.meaning: commercial ... are sales reps who go from town to town
the proverb says travel broadens the mind, so those who journey are broad-minded

explanation.surface: A remark that reps on the road are said to be open-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: Sales reps on the road were called commercial travellers, and the proverb makes journeyers broad-minded.

clue.text: Obstacle race

definitions.meaning: a horse race in which runners carry weights to even their chances

explanation.surface: A steeplechase with hurdles in the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Both an impediment and a weighted horse race in which better runners carry extra burden.

clue.text: Valentino miscast in unconventional work

indicators.note: actors who are miscast are put in the wrong roles, so the letters are put in the wrong places

explanation.surface: The silent film star badly cast in an avant-garde production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miscast' rearranges VALENTINO, the silent screen idol's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A novel that rejects the conventions of plot and character is an experimental piece of writing.

clue.text: Watch part being set up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to set something down is to lay it, past tense laid

explanation.surface: A component of a wristwatch being assembled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link; 'up' turns LAID round.
explanation.definitionFit: The face of a watch with its numerals is the dial.

clue.text: Goldsmith's political group in Irish capital

parts.note: a cell is a small unit of activists within a party

indicators.note: a capital letter is a word's first, so the opening letter of Irish

explanation.surface: A craftsman belongs to a party cell in Dublin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irish capital' looks like Dublin but gives only I. Benvenuto Cellini was a Renaissance goldsmith and sculptor.
explanation.definitionFit: Benvenuto Cellini was a famous Florentine sculptor and metalworker of the Renaissance.

clue.text: Do divide last of money

parts.note: to part is to separate or divide

indicators.note: the final letter of the word money is taken

explanation.surface: An instruction to split the remaining cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' is the definition, a noun meaning a celebration, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A do is informal for a social gathering or celebration.

clue.text: Tumbled down mountain

definitions.meaning: past tense of fall, meaning dropped to the ground
a hill or mountain in the north of England, especially the Lake District

explanation.surface: Someone took a tumble on a mountainside.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the past of fall and a northern English word for a hill.

clue.text: Descent by cable taking time

parts.note: a cable is a line, as in a telephone line
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Climbing down using a rope takes a long while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Descent' suggests going down a rope but means ancestry; 'by' and 'taking' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Descent in the sense of ancestry is one's line of forebears.

clue.text: What may be behind car advertisement

definitions.meaning: a towed vehicle or caravan hitched to the back of a car
a short preview of a film shown to promote it

explanation.surface: Something towed behind a car carrying an advert.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a towed wagon and a film preview used for publicity.

clue.text: Jumble in piles outside one's room

indicators.note: the word for piles sits outside, around the other pieces

parts.note: piles of things means many of them
one is I, and one's gives I'S, the apostrophe dropped
a cell is a small room, as in a monastery or prison

explanation.surface: A muddle of things heaped up outside someone's bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piles' looks like a noun for heaps; read it as a quantity word. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscellany is a mixed collection, a hotchpotch of assorted items.

clue.text: Minute can last interminably, so to speak

parts.note: a can is a tin

indicators.note: the final letter of the word interminably is taken

explanation.surface: A tin that lasts for ever, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' looks like a verb meaning endure but takes Y, the last letter of 'interminably'; 'so to speak' only flags the playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Minute, pronounced my-NEWT, means very small.

clue.text: Instrument's bent, and vile to listen to

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: when heard, the phrase sounds like something else

parts.note: bent double means folded over, and base means vile or low

explanation.surface: A musical instrument is warped and sounds dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: BASE (vile) said aloud is BASS, so DOUBLE BASE is heard as the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the largest member of the violin family, played standing.

clue.text: Many a variety of lily in one cold frame — how picturesque!

indicators.note: the two outer pieces form a frame around the middle ones

parts.note: one is I in Roman numerals
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
D is 500 in Roman numerals, so many

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so the letters of lily are rearranged

explanation.surface: A garden cold frame full of lilies makes a charming scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety of' rearranges LILY to YLLI. 'Many' giving D (500) is a Roman-numeral convention; 'in' and 'how' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: An idyllic scene is charming and pastoral, as pretty as a painting.

clue.text: Animals rescue rat after accident

indicators.note: after an accident things are wrecked and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wildlife saves a rodent after a mishap.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a rescue after a crash; 'after accident' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Creatures are living beings, beasts in general.

clue.text: Strings required, so quartet holds nothing back

indicators.note: the whole assembled run is read backwards
one word holds another, keeping it inside

parts.note: taken as written
nil means nothing, zero
IV is four in Roman numerals, a quartet

explanation.surface: A string quartet needs instruments, so keeps nothing in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the whole of SNILOIV round. 'required' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The violin family make up an orchestra's string section.

clue.text: Mount horse and get aid for players

parts.note: to mount a play is to stage it
H is slang for heroin, known as horse
taken as written

explanation.surface: Get on a horse and fetch help for the team.
explanation.walkthrough: H for horse: both are slang for heroin. 'get' is a link; 'players' are actors, not sportsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre worker who shifts scenery helps the actors on stage.

clue.text: Warning to fighter as grenade explodes

indicators.note: when something explodes it is blown apart, so these letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A soldier is alerted as a bomb goes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explodes' rearranges GRENADE; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The fencing call means be on guard, a caution to an opponent before a bout.

clue.text: Means of identification held up for security worker

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a name tag or badge shows who someone is

explanation.surface: An ID badge is shown to a guard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' turns NAME TAG round; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A gatekeeper guards an entrance, checking who passes.

clue.text: Land in Africa, having left part of Europe

parts.note: Iberia is the peninsula of Spain and Portugal

explanation.surface: Someone emigrates to an African country, leaving southern Europe behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' is a link joining L to IBERIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberia is a West African republic founded by freed American slaves.

clue.text: Greek drink in unopened container turned over

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned over means read backwards
the opening letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a canister is a metal container

explanation.surface: Greek wine kept in a sealed tin that has been upended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unopened' drops the first letter of CANISTER to give ANISTER, and 'turned over' reverses it; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: May first, for example, take girl out

definitions.meaning: a day of the calendar such as 1 May
to go on a romantic outing with someone

explanation.surface: Plans to go out with a girl on the first of May.
explanation.definitionFit: It means both a calendar day and a romantic outing with someone.

clue.text: Produce current stoppage without union, in fact

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a dam stops the current of a river
TU is the abbreviation for trade union

explanation.surface: A factory output halted by a power cut, with no union involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside. 'Produce' reads as an instruction to make the result, and 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A datum is a single piece of information, one given item of data.

clue.text: Insect finds source of sugar left in coach

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the word for coach

parts.note: a stage, short for stagecoach, is a horse-drawn coach
sugar beet is a crop sugar is made from

explanation.surface: A bug discovers sugar abandoned on a bus.
explanation.walkthrough: A stage, from stagecoach, is a horse-drawn coach that ran in stages; 'finds' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A large beetle whose males bear antler-like jaws.

clue.text: Possible outcome of hitting a sharp piece

indicators.note: a piece is a part, so the answer is a part of the words hitting a sharp

parts.note: striking a pointed or bladed object may leave a deep cut in the skin

explanation.surface: Striking something pointed may well leave a wound.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a description of an injury, but the answer sits inside 'hittinG A SHarp'; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep cut is a likely result of striking something keen-edged.

clue.text: Beat up for sport

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to flog is to beat

explanation.surface: Someone is beaten up for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns FLOG round; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf is a game played with clubs on a course.

clue.text: It'll provide beat to rumba wildly

indicators.note: dancing wildly suggests disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something keeps rhythm for frantic Latin dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' rearranges TO RUMBA.
explanation.definitionFit: A tambour is a drum, which keeps the rhythm.

clue.text: Parts of flowers showing ability to survive

definitions.meaning: a plural of stamen, the pollen-bearing organ of a flower

explanation.surface: Petals and pistils show how hardy a plant is.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an old plural of stamen and also a word for endurance.

clue.text: Like a brother, protecting female swimmer

indicators.note: the outer word protects the other by surrounding it

parts.note: a brother is a monk, so monkish means like one

explanation.surface: A monk-like man shelters a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protecting' puts F inside MONKISH; 'swimmer' is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A monkfish is an ugly sea fish, also called the angler.

clue.text: Man or no man?

definitions.meaning: the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea
from John Donne's line that no man is one, entire of itself

explanation.surface: A riddle asking whether something is a man or not.
explanation.definitionFit: Man is a land mass in the Irish Sea, and Donne wrote that no man is one.
